mainTopic: How the wording of a נדר decides whether it works: קרבן wordings, a קונם placed on one's limbs, and the opening of פרק ב on vows that compare food to things forbidden by the Torah.
overview: The amud opens with the גמרא settling a contradiction about the word קרבן. Saying 'הָא קָרְבָּן' sounds like swearing 'by the life of the offering', which does nothing, while 'הַקָּרְבָּן' is a real נדר. Next, the גמרא asks how רבי מאיר can forbid someone who said 'לַקָּרְבָּן לֹא אוֹכַל לָךְ', since he does not draw a 'yes' out of a 'no'. רבי אבא answers that the words mean 'let it be a קרבן, so I won't eat yours.' A new משנה rules that a קונם on 'my mouth speaking with you', 'my hand working with you' or 'my foot walking with you' takes effect. The גמרא challenges this from a ברייתא saying נדרים apply only to things with ממש. רב יהודה answers that the vow is placed on the physical mouth, hands and feet, and the משנה's wording supports him. The first פרק then ends. The second פרק opens with a משנה listing vows that fail because they compare food to things forbidden by the Torah rather than by a vow. The גמרא infers that saying 'לַחוּלִּין' would make a vow, then begins asking whether that fits רבי מאיר, a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two different wordings: 'הָא קָרְבָּן' versus 'הַקָּרְבָּן'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles an earlier contradiction about the word קרבן by saying the two sources are talking about two different wordings.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difficulty. One source is talking about someone who said 'הָא קָרְבָּן' (two words), and the other is talking about someone who said 'הַקָּרְבָּן' (one word, 'the offering').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a contradiction it raised just before this point by showing that each source is talking about a different way of saying the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction was about whether saying 'קרבן' creates a נדר. The answer is that the sources are not arguing. In one case the person said 'הָא קָרְבָּן', and in the other he said 'הַקָּרְבָּן'. A small difference in sound changes the legal result.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is the standard opening for an answer.
Two words: 'הָא' plus 'קָרְבָּן'. This wording does not create a נדר.
One word, 'the offering'. This wording does create a נדר.

steps.confusionAlert: 'הָא קָרְבָּן' and 'הַקָּרְבָּן' sound almost the same when said out loud, but the גמרא treats them as two different statements with two different results.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where he said 'ha korban',
phrases.notes: Here 'הָא' and 'קָרְבָּן' are two separate words. In the next line it's one word, 'הַקָּרְבָּן', meaning 'the offering'.

phrases.english: and that one is where he said 'hakorban'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction that was raised just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by wording): each source is talking about a different wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the sources disagreed about whether the word קרבן creates a נדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הָא קָרְבָּן' does not create a נדר, but 'הַקָּרְבָּן' does.

steps.title: Why 'הָא קָרְבָּן' does nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'הָא קָרְבָּן' means 'by the life of the offering', which is not a way to make a נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? He is saying 'by the life of the offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks itself why 'הָא קָרְבָּן' does not work, and answers that it sounds like swearing by the life of a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real נדר puts a forbidden status onto an object, as if that object were a קרבן. 'הָא קָרְבָּן' is heard as 'by the life of the קרבן', like swearing by something. That expression does not forbid anything, so no נדר takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
By the life of the offering

steps.whatToRemember: 'הַקָּרְבָּן' makes a real נדר. 'הָא קָרְבָּן' means 'by the life of the קרבן' and does nothing.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
He is saying 'by the life of the offering.'
phrases.notes: Saying 'by the life of' something is not a real way to make a נדר, so nothing takes effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the distinction made in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does 'הָא קָרְבָּן' fail to create a נדר?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means 'by the life of the קרבן', which is not a valid way to make a נדר.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: רבי מאיר forbids 'לַקָּרְבָּן'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה where רבי מאיר forbids someone who said 'לַקָּרְבָּן לֹא אוֹכַל לָךְ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches: if someone says 'Lakorban, I will not eat of yours', רבי מאיר forbids him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question by quoting a line from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לַקָּרְבָּן לֹא אוֹכַל לָךְ' can be heard as 'לא קרבן', meaning 'what I don't eat of yours is not a קרבן'. Read that way, he is hinting that whatever he does eat is a קרבן. רבי מאיר forbids the food, and the גמרא is about to ask how that fits with רבי מאיר's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches; this introduces a quote from the משנה
The vow wording that can be heard as 'לא קרבן', 'not a קרבן'
Forbids

phrases.english: It teaches:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting our משנה.

phrases.english: 'Lakorban, I will not eat of yours,'
Rabbi Meir prohibits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a different line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר forbids the food when someone says 'לַקָּרְבָּן לֹא אוֹכַל לָךְ'.

steps.title: But רבי מאיר doesn't draw a 'yes' from a 'no'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's ruling, because he holds that you cannot infer a positive statement from a negative one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't רבי מאיר hold that you cannot hear a 'yes' from a 'no'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling from step 3 by pointing out that it seems to go against רבי מאיר's own known principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To forbid the food, we would have to reason: 'he said what I don't eat is not a קרבן, so what I do eat is a קרבן.' That is drawing a 'yes' out of a 'no' (מכלל לאו אתה שומע הן). רבי מאיר does not accept that kind of reasoning, so how can he forbid the food?

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't he not hold? (an opening for a challenge)
From a 'no' you can hear a 'yes': an implied positive drawn from a negative statement

phrases.english: But doesn't Rabbi Meir not hold
that from a 'no' you can hear a 'yes'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רבי מאיר quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling forbidding 'לַקָּרְבָּן לֹא אוֹכַל לָךְ'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems to depend on drawing a 'yes' out of a 'no', which רבי מאיר himself rejects.

steps.title: רבי אבא: read it as 'Let it be a קרבן, so I won't eat'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that the words mean 'let it be a קרבן, and so I will not eat yours.' That is a direct positive statement, so no 'yes from a no' is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: It is as if he said, 'Let it be for a קרבן, and therefore I will not eat of yours.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the challenge by reading the person's words in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא does not read the word as 'לא קרבן' ('not a קרבן'). He reads it as 'לְקָרְבָּן', meaning 'let your food be a קרבן'. 'I will not eat of yours' is then just the result. Because the person stated the forbidding directly, רבי מאיר's rule against inferring a 'yes' from a 'no' never comes into play.

keyTerms.meaning: It becomes as if he said
Let it be for a קרבן
Therefore

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אבא, 'לַקָּרְבָּן לֹא אוֹכַל לָךְ' means 'let it be a קרבן, so I won't eat.' It is a direct נדר, not a hint.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
It is as though he said:
'Let it be for an offering,'
therefore I will not eat of yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the vow wording as a direct positive statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the vow worked only by drawing a 'yes' out of 'not a קרבן'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words mean 'let it be a קרבן', a direct statement, so it fits רבי מאיר.

steps.title: New משנה: a קונם on speaking, working or walking with someone
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a קונם on one's mouth speaking, hand working, or foot walking with another person takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says to his friend, 'קונם, my mouth speaking with you', or 'my hand working with you', or 'my foot walking with you', he is forbidden to do so.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that a נדר can forbid actions like talking, working or walking with someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person here does not forbid any food or object. He forbids his own actions with his friend. The משנה says this works, and the גמרא will now question that.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A substitute word for קרבן, used to make a נדר
To his friend
Forbidden

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who says to his fellow:
'Konam, my mouth speaking with you,'
'my hand working with you,'
'my foot walking with you'
he is prohibited.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ קֻוֽנָּם פִּי מְדַבֵּר עִמָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קונם on one's mouth, hand or foot acting with another person takes effect.

steps.title: A ברייתא says נדרים only apply to things with substance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts the משנה with a ברייתא listing the strictures of נדרים and שבועות. The ברייתא says only שבועות apply to things without physical substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: There is a stricture in שבועות beyond נדרים, and in נדרים beyond שבועות. The stricture of נדרים: they take effect on a מצוה just as on an optional matter, which is not so with שבועות. The stricture of שבועות: they take effect on a thing that has substance and a thing that has no substance, which is not so with נדרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new משנה by quoting a ברייתא that seems to say a נדר cannot apply to actions like speaking or walking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a נדר can forbid a מצוה item, which a שבועה cannot do. A שבועה, however, works even on things without ממש (physical substance), and a נדר does not. Speaking, working and walking are actions, not physical objects. So by the ברייתא, the נדר in our משנה should not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that comes after the משנה
And they raised a contradiction: two sources are set against each other
A stricture; a way one thing is stricter than another
An optional matter (not a מצוה)
Physical substance

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic difference: a נדר needs something with ממש to take effect on, while a שבועה does not. רב יהודה's answer in Step 8 depends on that difference.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And they raised a contradiction:
There is a stricture in oaths beyond vows
and in vows beyond oaths.
The stricture in vows:
that vows take effect on a מצוה just as on an optional matter,
which is not so with oaths.
And the stricture in oaths:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַשְּׁבוּעוֹת חָלוֹת עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ
phrases.english: that oaths take effect on a thing that has substance
and on one that has no substance,
which is not so with vows.
phrases.notes: Speaking or walking is not a physical thing. That is exactly why this clashes with our משנה.

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a קונם on speaking, working or walking takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says נדרים do not apply to things without ממש. Speech and actions have no ממש, so the נדר should not work.

steps.title: The vow is placed on the limb itself
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the משנה is talking about someone who forbids his actual mouth, hands, or feet, which are physical things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The משנה means someone who says, 'My mouth shall be forbidden to my speech,' 'My hands to their work,' or 'My feet to their walking.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the contradiction from Step 7 by explaining exactly what the person in the משנה said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a נדר cannot take effect on something with no physical substance, like speaking or walking. רב יהודה says the person did not forbid the action. He forbade his mouth, hands, or feet, which are real physical body parts, so a נדר can take effect on them.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here
Shall be forbidden
Speech
Walking

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
It is a case where he says: 'My mouth shall be forbidden to my speech,'
'My hands to their work,'
'My feet to their walking.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא raised in Step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to let a נדר take effect on speaking, working, and walking, which have no physical substance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow is on the mouth, hands, and feet themselves, which are physical, so the נדר takes effect.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה says 'my mouth speaking with you' and not 'that I speak with you,' which fits רב יהודה's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also precise in the משנה, because it says 'my mouth speaking with you' and does not say 'that I speak with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב יהודה by showing that the exact wording of the משנה matches his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה meant the act of speaking, it would have said 'that I speak with you.' It mentions 'my mouth' instead, which shows the vow is on the body part. So רב יהודה's answer is not forced. It is built into the משנה's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise: the wording supports this
It teaches; the משנה says

steps.whatToRemember: A נדר takes effect only on something physical. 'My mouth' is physical, but 'my speaking' is not. That is how the משנה and the ברייתא fit together.

phrases.english: It is also precise in the language,
since it teaches: 'my mouth speaking with you,'
and it does not teach: 'that I speak with you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's answer from the wording of the משנה
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's explanation that the vow is on the limb
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact wording of the משנה: 'פי מדבר עמך' rather than 'שאני מדבר עמך'

steps.title: Hadran: closing the chapter כל כינויי
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of נדרים ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter כל כינויי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line that marks the end of the first פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'הדרן עלך' mean 'we will return to you.' Learners say this when they finish a פרק. The next line starts a new פרק with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: said when finishing a chapter
Name of the first פרק of נדרים

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter Kol Kinnuyei

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the chapter after the final discussion
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of מסכת נדרים is complete.

steps.title: Vows that compare food to Torah-forbidden things do not work
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists vows that fail: calling food חולין, or comparing it to pig meat, עבודה זרה, נבילות, שקצים, or the חלה and תרומה of אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these vows leave the food permitted: 'What I eat of yours will be חולין,' 'like pig meat,' 'like עבודה זרה,' 'like hides with the heart cut out,' 'like נבילות and טריפות,' 'like שקצים and רמשים,' 'like the חלה of אהרן and his תרומה.' In all these cases the food is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The second פרק opens with a משנה listing vows that do not take effect at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make a נדר, you compare an item to something that is forbidden because of a vow, like a קרבן. Pig meat, נבילות, and the rest are forbidden by the Torah itself, not by a vow. So comparing food to them creates no prohibition. Calling food 'חולין' fails for a simpler reason: חולין is ordinary and permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Permitted: the vow does not take effect
Ordinary, non-holy food
Hides of animals offered to idols, with a hole cut at the heart
Animals that died without שחיטה, and fatally wounded animals
Holy portions given to כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: These items are all forbidden to eat, yet the vow still fails. The issue is not whether the item is forbidden. It is whether it is forbidden because of a vow.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic rule of the new פרק: a נדר must be tied to something forbidden through a vow, like a קרבן.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are permitted:
'What I eat of yours will be non-sacred,'
'like pig meat,' 'like idol worship,'
'like hides with the heart cut out,'
phrases.notes: These are hides of animals offered to idols. A hole was cut at the heart and the heart was taken out.

phrases.english: 'like carcasses and fatally wounded animals,'
'like repugnant creatures and creeping animals,'
'like the challa of Aaron and his teruma': it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the Hadran
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vows that call food חולין, or compare it to things forbidden by the Torah, do not take effect, and the food stays permitted.

steps.title: A man who compares his wife to his mother
steps.stepSummary: If a man tells his wife 'you are to me like my mother,' a חכם still releases him, using a different opening, so that he does not take vows lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone tells his wife, 'You are to me like my mother,' they open a way of release for him from a different angle, so that he will not treat vows lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case: a vow comparing one's wife to one's mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier cases, his mother is forbidden by the Torah, not by a vow, so this vow should not really work. Even so, the משנה requires a חכם to release him. This teaches him not to be careless with vows.

keyTerms.meaning: Like my mother
They open an opening: a חכם finds a way to release the vow
So that he will not be lighthearted, meaning careless about vows

steps.whatToRemember: The new משנה teaches that a vow must be tied to something forbidden by a vow, not by the Torah. In the wife-and-mother case, the חכמים still require a release so that people stay careful with vows.

phrases.english: One who says to his wife,
'You are hereby to me like my mother':
they open an opening for him from a different place.
phrases.notes: An 'opening' is a reason a חכם uses to release a vow. Here the חכם uses a different reason, not the fact that the vow never worked.

phrases.english: so that he will not take this lightly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related case where the vow does not truly work, but a release is still required
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who says to his wife 'you are to me like my mother' needs a release from a חכם through a different opening, so that he does not treat vows lightly.

steps.title: The vow fails only because he said 'חולין'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. The vow fails only because he said 'חולין'. Saying 'לחולין' (not חולין) would imply 'קרבן' and would be a valid vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה's vow fails because the person said 'חולין is what I eat of yours'. But if he said 'לחולין (not חולין) is what I eat of yours', that implies: let it not be ordinary, but a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the new משנה by pointing out what its wording implies. A slightly different wording, 'לחולין', would make the vow work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying food is 'חולין', meaning ordinary, does not forbid anything, so the vow fails. The גמרא reads 'לחולין' as 'לא חולין', meaning not ordinary. Saying 'not ordinary' suggests the opposite, 'holy like a קרבן', and that does forbid the food. This inference sets up the next question about whose view the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason; here it means 'the only reason the vow fails is...'
Ordinary, non-holy food
Read here as 'לא חולין', meaning 'not ordinary'
An offering; food called this becomes forbidden like a holy offering
It implies, it means

steps.confusionAlert: 'לחולין' here does not mean 'for חולין'. The גמרא hears it as 'לא חולין', meaning 'not חולין', which is the opposite.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason [the vow fails] is that he said
'Chullin is what I eat of yours'
But if he said 'lachullin is what I eat of yours'
it implies: let it not be chullin
but rather a korban

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאָמַר ״חוּלִּין שֶׁאוֹכַל לָךְ״ הָא אָמַר ״לַחוּלִּין שֶׁאוֹכַל לָךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה from Step 11 by drawing an inference from its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'חולין' does not create a vow. Saying 'לחולין' (not חולין) implies קרבן and does create a vow.

steps.title: Whose opinion does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows. It begins to test רבי מאיר, who does not draw a 'yes' from a 'no'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? If it is רבי מאיר, doesn't he hold that from a negative statement [you do not infer the positive]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows and starts to check whether it could be רבי מאיר. This line sets up a challenge that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference in Step 13 depends on hearing 'not חולין' as meaning 'yes, קרבן'. That is inferring a positive from a negative. רבי מאיר is known not to accept that kind of inference, so the משנה would be hard to explain as his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is the משנה?
He does not hold
From the implication of a statement; the start of 'מכלל לאו אתה שומע הן', 'from a no you hear a yes'

phrases.english: Whose opinion is the Mishnah?
If it is Rabbi Meir
doesn't he not hold that from [a negative statement]
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next amud: 'you can infer the positive'. רבי מאיר rejects that kind of inference.
